question: What is the main sign that a patient is truly unconscious?

options.A: A state of deep sleep that ends easily with noise
options.C: Inability to speak while remaining fully awake
options.D: Temporary dizziness upon standing up quickly

explanation: You've got this! Unconsciousness simply means the person cannot respond at all to what is happening around them. Keep going! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h1)

question: How is locked-in syndrome different from true unconsciousness?

options.A: The patient experiences brief episodes of total memory loss
options.B: The patient responds only to painful physical pressure
options.C: The patient is fully aware but unable to move or speak
options.D: The patient sleeps for most of the day and night

explanation: Great job! In locked-in syndrome, their mind is completely awake and aware inside, they just can't move their muscles or talk. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which part of the brain acts like the main switchboard to keep us awake?
explanation: Think of the reticular activating system in the brainstem as the master 'wake-up' switch for the whole brain. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h2)

question: What usually happens if a patient's thinking part of the brain is badly damaged, but their brainstem is totally fine?

options.A: The patient loses awareness of the environment but may still sleep and wake
options.B: The patient loses all reflex actions while keeping clear thoughts
options.C: The patient stays completely awake but loses the ability to feel pain
options.D: The patient enters an immediate state of permanent brain death

explanation: You're doing great! Because the brainstem handles sleep-wake cycles, an undamaged brainstem means the body can still cycle between sleeping and waking up, even without higher thinking. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which body problem is a very common cause of sudden confusion or unconsciousness?
explanation: Spot on! When blood sugar drops too low (hypoglycemia), the brain gets starved of its main energy source and shuts down fast. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h3)

question: If someone falls into a coma from taking way too much of a drug or poison, what kind of cause is that?
explanation: You nailed it! Poisons and overdoses travel through the blood to chemically depress brain activity, rather than physically crushing the brain tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h3)

question: What dangerous event happens when severe swelling inside the skull pushes brain tissue downward?
explanation: Brain herniation is a medical emergency where high pressure forces brain tissue to shift where it shouldn't go. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why is a rise in pressure inside the skull so harmful to the brain?

options.A: It immediately destroys the myelin sheath surrounding peripheral nerves
options.B: It triggers an excessive production of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles
options.C: It causes the skull bones to expand and fracture outward
options.D: It squeezes blood vessels and reduces the flow of oxygen to brain cells

explanation: Makes total sense, right? The skull can't stretch, so high pressure squeezes the tiny blood vessels shut, cutting off vital oxygen to brain cells. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h4)

question: What three things does the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) check?

options.A: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.B: Heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure
options.D: Pupil reaction, temperature, and skin color

explanation: You've got this! GCS is a quick way to grade brain function by checking if the patient opens their eyes, talks, and moves. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h5)

question: If a nurse shines a light in an unconscious patient's eyes and both pupils stay large and don't react, what does that usually mean?

options.A: Dangerous pressure is affecting the brainstem
options.B: The patient is experiencing a mild concussion
options.C: Blood glucose levels are extremely elevated
options.D: The patient is entering a normal deep sleep cycle

explanation: Good catch! Fixed, unmoving pupils are a serious warning sign that pressure is squeezing the vital brainstem pathways. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which quick bedside test must you do immediately for any unconscious patient?
explanation: Always check the sugar first! Low blood sugar can mimic a major stroke or brain injury, and it's super easy to test and fix right at the bedside. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why do doctors urgently order a CT scan of the head for a patient who suddenly becomes unconscious?

options.A: To quickly spot bleeding, blood clots, or structural brain damage
options.B: To measure the exact electrical activity firing across the cortex
options.C: To check for bacterial growth within the cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: To determine if the patient has ingested specific toxic drugs

explanation: Brilliant! A CT scan gives a fast, clear picture to see if there is dangerous bleeding or a blood clot that needs immediate attention. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is the main reason for putting an artificial airway in an unconscious patient?

options.A: To prevent the tongue from sliding back during feeding
options.B: To allow the administration of oral liquid medications
options.C: To protect against aspiration and maintain clear breathing
options.D: To measure core body temperature continuously

explanation: You're doing great! Unconscious patients can't protect their airway or swallow properly, so a tube keeps air flowing and stops saliva or vomit from entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why do nurses usually keep the head of the bed slightly elevated for a patient with high brain pressure?

options.A: To allow clearer visibility during frequent neurological checks
options.B: To help blood drain away from the head and lower pressure
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to swallow saliva safely
options.D: To prevent the lungs from collapsing during mechanical ventilation

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Elevating the head helps blood flow smoothly out of the brain, keeping intracranial pressure down. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which nursing care helps stop joint stiffness in an unconscious patient?

options.C: Keeping the patient flat on the back
options.D: Applying warm compresses to the chest

explanation: Spot on! Gently moving their arms and legs through their normal motion keeps the joints flexible while they can't move on their own. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal complication of being unconscious and immobile for a long time?

options.B: Deep vein thrombosis in the lower legs
options.D: Rapid spontaneous recovery of cognitive speech

explanation: You got it! Prolonged unconsciousness causes physical problems like blood clots and stiff joints, rather than a sudden, magical recovery of speech. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h8)
